exposure: Time interval from MBS to birth (within 18 months vs. 18+ months)
cohort: Women with severe obesity in New York State, categorized by whether they underwent metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) or not, identified from hospital discharge databases.
finding: While MBS may reduce adverse maternal nonbirth outcomes and pregnancy complications in women with obesity, neonates born to women who conceived within the first year after MBS, especially RYGB, may face a higher risk for adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: Post-MBS mothers generally had a lower incidence of cesarean deliveries compared to No-MBS mothers, but within the Post-MBS group, deliveries within 18 months after surgery and pregnancies after RYGB were associated with higher rates of cesarean sections.
